summary: Retire the public legacy API hostname dependency and make https://ekodi.kr/api the single canonical public EKODI API base while keeping the Control Worker behind private service binding.
approvalBasis: The EKODI Platform Super Administrator explicitly instructed EKODI to continue with the https://ekodi.kr/api structure and complete the migration under EKODI orchestration.
constitutionalInterpretation: This tightens the existing apex-path-only and zero-subdomain policy without expanding autonomous authority. Internal service boundaries, authentication, permissions, guarded release, rollback and production verification remain mandatory.
implementedCapabilities: Removal of the legacy API custom-domain exposure
Apex health and API discovery endpoints
Runtime, admin, monitoring and release references migrated to apex API
Canonical MCP resource retained at https://ekodi.kr/mcp
Audited migration of legacy MCP authorization resource records
Zero-subdomain guard strengthened for migration-removal diffs
authorityImpact: None. No permission, identity, legal, financial or high-risk authority is expanded.
deploymentImpact: Control API remains the same internal Worker and D1 boundary, but public traffic enters through ekodi.kr/api via the Shared Site CONTROL_API service binding. The legacy API custom domain is removed only after guarded verification.
rollback: If apex production verification fails, restore the previous Control Worker route only as an emergency rollback, repair the apex binding, then re-run guarded verification before retiring the legacy host again. No compatibility redirect is introduced.
